title: Dynamic factor models
text: compare three models known loadings, simulated six series three AR(1) trends. Trend 1 strongly autocorrelated (ϕ1=0.85\phi_1 = 0.85) drives series 1 3. Trend 2 weakly autocorrelated (ϕ2=0.15\phi_2 = 0.15) drives series 4 5. Trend 3 (ϕ3=0.55\phi_3 = 0.55) largest innovation SD drives series 6 alone. last 15 80 time points held . mvgam_data() checks training data plots series, held-points black: six simulated series. Series 1 3 follow one trend, series 4 5 second, series 6 third. Black points dashed line held .
code: set.seed(3)  n_time <- 80 n_series <- 6 n_lv <- 3 n_train <- 65 phi_true <- c(0.85, 0.15, 0.55) sig_true <- c(0.5, 0.35, 0.8)  # Each trend starts at its stationary distribution lv <- matrix(NA, n_time, n_lv) lv[1, ] <- rnorm(n_lv, 0, sig_true / sqrt(1 - phi_true^2)) for (t in 2:n_time) {   lv[t, ] <- phi_true * lv[t - 1L, ] + rnorm(n_lv, 0, sig_true) }  # Series 1-3 load on trend 1, series 4-5 on trend 2, series 6 on trend 3 Z_true <- matrix(0, nrow = n_series, ncol = n_lv) Z_true[cbind(1:6, c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3))] <- 1  # Observations add Gaussian noise with SD 0.2 y_mat <- lv %*% t(Z_true) +   matrix(rnorm(n_time * n_series, 0, 0.2), n_time, n_series)  sim_data <- data.frame(   time = rep(seq_len(n_time), n_series),   series = factor(     rep(paste0("s", seq_len(n_series)), each = n_time),     levels = paste0("s", seq_len(n_series))   ),   y = as.numeric(y_mat) ) train <- sim_data[sim_data$time <= n_train, ] test  <- sim_data[sim_data$time >  n_train, ] mvgam_data(train, family = gaussian(), trend_formula = ~ AR(),            newdata = test)

Counts along route surveyed effort EtE_t Poisson mean λtEt\lambda_t E_t. term offset(log_effort) carries effort. occupancy survey plot area AA detects species least one individual present. Poisson number individuals plot, detection probability pt=1−exp⁡(−λtA)p_t = 1 - \exp(-\lambda_t ). inverse complementary log-log link, cloglog(pt)=log⁡λt+log⁡\text{cloglog}(p_t) = \log \lambda_t + \log (McCullagh Nelder 1989). bernoulli(link = "cloglog"), occupancy record shares log-intensity counts, offset log⁡\log . Opportunistic sightings arrive rate λt\lambda_t thinned unknown, constant observer effort. Treated thinned Poisson process, take free intercept absorbs log thinning leaves shape ff identified (Fithian et al. 2015; Renner et al. 2015).
code: set.seed(2026) n_t <- 96 env <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(n_t, 0, 0.3)))) f_env <- function(x) 1.5 * exp(-0.5 * (x - 0.4)^2) - 0.4  z <- numeric(n_t) for (t in seq_len(n_t)) {   z[t] <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.35) +     (if (t > 1) 0.55 * z[t - 1] else 0) +     (if (t > 12) 0.30 * z[t - 12] else 0) } lambda <- exp(0.5 + f_env(env) + z)  effort <- runif(n_t, 0.5, 2) area <- 0.25 log_thinning <- -0.8  idm_data <- data.frame(   time = seq_len(n_t),   series = factor("species1"),   env = env,   log_effort = log(effort),   count = rpois(n_t, lambda * effort),   pa = rbinom(n_t, 1, 1 - exp(-lambda * area)),   po = rpois(n_t, lambda * exp(log_thinning)) )

f_env(grid[ref])) curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {   q <- apply(fits[[nm]], 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))   data.frame(model = nm, env = grid, lo = q[1, ], med = q[2, ],              hi = q[3, ]) })) curves$model <- factor(curves$model, levels = names(fits)) ggplot(curves, aes(env)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "#DCBCBC") +   geom_line(aes(y = med), colour = "#8F2727", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_line(aes(y = f), data = truth, linewidth = 0.6) +   facet_wrap(~ model) +   labs(x = "env", y = "Shift in log-intensity") recovery <- t(vapply(fits, function(draws) {   q <- apply(draws, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))   peak <- grid[apply(draws, 1, which.max)]   c(RMSE = sqrt(mean((q[2, ] - truth$f)^2)),     `Interval width` = mean(q[3, ] - q[1, ]),     `Peak env` = median(peak)) }, numeric(3))) round(recovery, 2) #>                 RMSE Interval width Peak env #> Joint           0.18           0.67     0.38 #> Counts alone    0.18           0.74     0.32 #> Occupancy alone 0.63           1.17     2.02 #> Sightings alone 0.42           0.88     1.14

title: One latent process, several observation models
text: latent abundance ztz_t, log scale, follows stationary AR(1) 80 months: zt∼Normal(0.7zt−1,0.4). z_t \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0.7\, z_{t-1},\ 0.4). Three methods observe . Transect counts (count) Poisson log link. Survey effort varies month enters offset. Trap biomass (biomass) Gamma log link shape 2. seasonal cycle month adds latent state. Camera detections (camera) Bernoulli logit link. Detection rises 0.05 logit scale day camera deployed. cameras run 60 80 months. three simulated monitoring records. camera record gaps months cameras run.
code: set.seed(2024) n_time <- 80 z <- numeric(n_time) z[1] <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.4 / sqrt(1 - 0.7^2)) for (t in 2:n_time) {   z[t] <- 0.7 * z[t - 1] + rnorm(1, 0, 0.4) }  month <- (seq_len(n_time) - 1) %% 12 + 1 log_effort <- log(runif(n_time, 0.8, 1.2)) deploy_days <- runif(n_time, 5, 20) mu_biomass <- exp(0.5 + sin(2 * pi * month / 12) + z)  mv_data <- data.frame(   time = seq_len(n_time),   series = factor("pop1"),   month = month,   log_effort = log_effort,   deploy_days = deploy_days,   count = rpois(n_time, exp(1.5 + log_effort + z)),   biomass = rgamma(n_time, shape = 2, rate = 2 / mu_biomass),   camera = rbinom(n_time, 1, plogis(-0.5 + 0.05 * deploy_days + z)) ) mv_data$camera[-sort(sample.int(n_time, 60))] <- NA observed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("count", "biomass", "camera"), function(r) {   data.frame(time = mv_data$time, value = mv_data[[r]], response = r) })) observed$response <- factor(observed$response,                             levels = c("count", "biomass", "camera")) ggplot(observed, aes(time, value)) +   geom_line(data = ~ subset(.x, response != "camera"), colour = "#A25050") +   geom_point(size = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +   facet_wrap(~ response, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   labs(x = "Month", y = NULL)

code: set.seed(11) n_sp <- 4 n_year <- 20 n_visit <- 5 species <- paste0("sp_", seq_len(n_sp))  # A yearly temperature index with mean 0 and SD 1 temp <- round(as.numeric(scale(   cumsum(rnorm(n_year, 0, 0.6)) + rnorm(n_year) )), 2)  # AR(1) deviations in log abundance that temperature leaves unexplained z <- matrix(0, n_year, n_sp) for (t in 2:n_year) z[t, ] <- 0.6 * z[t - 1, ] + rnorm(n_sp, 0, 0.2)  # Each species' response to temperature on the log scale: a # saturating rise, a hump, a decline and a weak U temp_effect <- cbind(   0.8 * tanh(1.5 * temp),   0.6 - 0.6 * temp^2,   -0.5 * temp,   0.2 * temp^2 - 0.2 )  # Abundance N each year, around baselines of 30, 12, 20 and 10 log_lambda <- sweep(temp_effect + z, 2, log(c(30, 12, 20, 10)), "+") N <- matrix(rpois(n_year * n_sp, exp(log_lambda)), n_year, n_sp)  # Logit detection intercept of each species det_sp <- rnorm(n_sp, 0.3, 0.4)  # One row per visit, with wind speed recorded on each dat <- expand.grid(visit = seq_len(n_visit), time = seq_len(n_year),                    series = factor(species, levels = species)) dat$temp <- temp[dat$time] dat$wind <- round(runif(nrow(dat)), 2) dat$N <- N[cbind(dat$time, as.integer(dat$series))]  # Each individual present is counted with probability p, which falls # with wind speed p <- plogis(det_sp[dat$series] - 1.5 * dat$wind) dat$y <- rbinom(nrow(dat), dat$N, p)  # Upper bound of the sum over N in each closure unit dat$cap <- 80L head(dat) #>   visit time series temp wind  N  y cap #> 1     1    1   sp_1 1.07 0.77 59 25  80 #> 2     2    1   sp_1 1.07 0.14 59 31  80 #> 3     3    1   sp_1 1.07 0.50 59 28  80 #> 4     4    1   sp_1 1.07 0.04 59 47  80 #> 5     5    1   sp_1 1.07 0.36 59 27  80 #> 6     1    2   sp_1 1.56 0.20 48 21  80 train <- subset(dat, time <= 17) test <- subset(dat, time > 17)

code: # \dontrun{ set.seed(1) dat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 2L,                  n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())$data_train  # Every prior the model takes, before any fitting. Trend classes # carry a `_trend` suffix: `b` belongs to the observation formula # and `b_trend` would belong to the trend formula. mf <- mvgam_formula(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1)) get_prior(mf, data = dat, family = poisson()) #>                   prior       class        coef group resp dpar nlpar lb ub tag #>  student_t(3, 1.4, 2.5)   Intercept                                             #>                  (flat)           b                                             #>                  (flat)           b        sx_1                                 #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds                                    0        #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds s(x, k = 5)                        0        #>          exponential(2) sigma_trend                                    0        #>          normal(0, 0.5)   ar1_trend                                   -1  1     #>        source #>       default #>       default #>  (vectorized) #>       default #>  (vectorized) #>       default #>       default  # Replace three defaults. Each `prior()` call gives one row. my_priors <- c(   prior(std_normal(), class = b),   prior(inv_gamma(5, 1), class = sigma_trend),   prior(normal(0.5, 0.25), class = ar1_trend) )  # `run_model = FALSE` builds the model without sampling. Its prior # table marks the replaced rows as "user". pre <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),              data = dat, family = poisson(), prior = my_priors,              run_model = FALSE) prior_summary(pre) #>                   prior       class        coef group resp dpar nlpar lb ub tag #>  student_t(3, 1.4, 2.5)   Intercept                                             #>            std_normal()           b                                             #>            std_normal()           b        sx_1                                 #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds                                    0        #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds s(x, k = 5)                        0        #>         inv_gamma(5, 1) sigma_trend                                    0        #>       normal(0.5, 0.25)   ar1_trend                                   -1  1     #>        source #>       default #>          user #>          user #>       default #>  (vectorized) #>          user #>          user  # Next, drop `run_model = FALSE` to fit the model under these priors # }

title: The equations of a model, as Markdown — methods_md
code: # \dontrun{ set.seed(13) simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,                      n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR()) mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),               data    = simdat$data_train,               family  = poisson(),               chains  = 2, silent = 2) #> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence. #> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.  # The equations, glossary and priors as Markdown md <- methods_md(mod) md #> ## Data #>  #> $y$: non-negative integer counts #>  #> $N = 90$ observations, $S = 1$ series, $T = 90$ time points #>  #> Predictors: #>  #> - $x$: continuous covariate #>  #> ## Model #>  #> $$ #> \begin{aligned} #> t &\in \{1, \ldots, 90\} \\ #> y_{i,t} &\sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{i,t}) \\ #> \log \mu_{i,t} &= \alpha + f_{x}(x_{i,t}) + \eta_{i,t} \\ #> f_{x}(x) &= \sum_{m=1}^{K_{x}} \beta^{(x)}_m B_m(x) \\ #> \eta_{i,t} &= \phi_{1} \eta_{i,t-1} + \epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t} \\ #> \epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_\eta) #> \end{aligned} #> $$ #>  #> where: #>  #> - $i$ indexes series, $t$ indexes time #> - $\mu_{i,t}$: conditional mean of $y_{i,t}$ #> - $\alpha$: population intercept #> - $f_{x}$: thin plate regression spline in $x$, basis size $K_{x}$ (mgcv default), smoothing SD $\sigma^{(s)}_{x}$ #> - $\eta_{i,t}$: latent state at series $i$ time $t$ #> - $\epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t}$: process innovation, SD $\sigma_\eta$ #> - $\phi_{l}$: autoregressive coefficient at lag $l$ #>  #> ## Priors #>  #> $$ #> \begin{aligned} #> \alpha &\sim \text{StudentT}(3, 1.6, 2.5) \\ #> \sigma^{(s)}_{x} &\sim \text{StudentT}(3, 0, 2.5) \\ #> \sigma_\eta &\sim \text{Exponential}(2) \\ #> \phi_{1} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 0.5) #> \end{aligned} #> $$ #>  #> Every other parameter takes an improper flat prior on its support. #>  #> ## Implementation #>  #> Fitted with mvgam 2.0.0 (brms 2.23.2; Stan 2.40.0 via cmdstanr). Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: 2 chains, 1000 warmup + 1000 sampling iterations per chain. #>  #> ``` #> mvgam( #>   formula       = y ~ s(x), #>   trend_formula = ~AR(p = 1), #>   data          = simdat$data_train, #>   family        = poisson(), #>   backend       = "cmdstanr", #>   chains        = 2, #>   iter          = 2000, #>   warmup        = 1000 #> ) #> ```  # Written to a file, nested under a level-two heading methods_md(mod, file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), heading_level = 3L)  # Next, how_to_cite() writes the methods paragraph # }

what: Multivariate models, single shared trend type

Different trend types per response (e.g. RW() one response AR(p = 3) another) supported added. mvgam stores latent trend states single lv_trend matrix shared dynamics parameters; mixing trend types per response require parallel dynamics machinery throughout codegen, sampling, prediction pipelines. multivariate models support: Different observation families per response (e.g. bf(count ~ x, family = poisson()) +     bf(biomass ~ x, family = Gamma())). Different fixed-effect, smooth, GP terms per response observation formulas. title: N-mixture family for repeated counts of unmarked individuals — nmix
text: three variants take N ~ Poisson(mu) differ visit records. "poisson_binomial" (Royle 2004) Counts y ~ Binomial(N, p), never exceed N. Point counts, removal passes plot tallies fit design. p detection probability individual, logit link. "royle_nichols" (Royle Nichols 2003) Detections y ~ Bernoulli(1 - (1 - p)^N) 0 / 1. Camera-trap eDNA detections scored present absent fit design. p detection probability individual, logit link. visit's detection probability rises N. "poisson_poisson" (Neyman 1939) Counts y ~ Poisson(N * p), can exceed N. Camera-trap events acoustic detections, one individual recorded several times, fit design. p encounter rate individual per visit, log link.

code: pivot_detection_array(   y,   site_covs = NULL,   season_covs = NULL,   site_season_covs = NULL,   obs_covs = NULL,   species = NULL,   site_col = "site",   season_col = "season",   visit_col = "visit",   time_col = "time",   series_col = "series",   y_col = "y",   multi_season = c("fused", "hierarchical") )

title: Pivot a detection array to mvgam long-format — pivot_detection_array
text: y One four layouts: Single-species, single-season: [J_sites, K_max_visits] matrix detections (0 / 1 occ(), non-negative counts nmix()). unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccu / unmarkedFramePCount y slot flocker::flock obs argument type = "single". Multi-species, single-season (array): [N_species, J_sites, K_max_visits] array. spOccupancy::lfMsPGOcc / msPGOcc y slot. Multi-species, single-season (list): named list [J_sites, K_max_visits] matrices, one per species. unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccuMulti y slot; list names become species labels. Multi-species, multi-season: [N_species, J_sites, T_seasons, K_max_visits] 4D array. spOccupancy::tMsPGOcc / svcTMsPGOcc y slot. single-species multi-season data, wrap length-1 list (list(only_species = matrix_or_3d_array)) pass [1, J, T, K] array. NA entries mark missing visits / seasons dropped output. site_covs Optional data.frame site-level covariates nrow == J_sites. Broadcast across visits, seasons species. unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccu siteCovs slot, spOccupancy occ.covs flocker unit_covs map . season_covs Optional data.frame season-level covariates nrow == T_seasons. Broadcast across sites, visits species. Use year--study effects, season--year covariates, covariate varies across primary periods constant within season. site_season_covs Optional named list [J_sites, T_seasons] matrices covariates vary across (site, season) interaction (e.g., site-level habitat changes seasons). obs_covs Optional visit-level covariates: Single-season: named list [J_sites, K_max_visits] matrices, long-format data.frame J_sites * K_max_visits rows site-major / visit-fastest order (unmarked obsCovs convention). Multi-season: named list [J_sites, T_seasons, K_max_visits] arrays. species Optional character vector species names length == N_species. meaningful multi-species y. y named list, list names take precedence. Defaults sp1, sp2, .... site_col Name site identifier output. Defaults "site". season_col Name season identifier output. Defaults "season". visit_col Name visit identifier. Defaults "visit". time_col Name closure-unit time identifier. Defaults "time". Single-season: time = site. Multi-season + multi_season = "fused": time = (site - 1) * T + season (one closure unit per (site, season)). Multi-season + multi_season = "hierarchical": time = season (one closure unit per (species, site, season), site referenced separately observation formula). series_col Name species column. Defaults "series". y_col Name detection / count column. Defaults "y". *_col arguments must name different output column. multi_season Character scalar controlling multi-season time encoding. "fused" (default) fuses (site, season) single time axis (site, season) pair unique closure unit. matches existing single-season closure-unit grouping (series, time) works occ() / nmix() unchanged. "hierarchical" keeps time = season exposes site side-car covariate use observation formula; pair occ(multi_season = TRUE) nmix(multi_season = TRUE) 3-axis closure-unit grouping (series, site, time) activated. Ignored single-season inputs (2D matrix, 3D [N, J, K] array, 4D array T = 1).

title: Pivot a detection array to mvgam long-format — pivot_detection_array
text: "fused" (default): time = (site - 1) * T + season, (site, season) pair unique closure-unit identifier. Use seasons independent given covariates (single-season analysis applied per season, cross-season dynamics modelled). "hierarchical": time = season. Pair occ(multi_season = TRUE) / nmix(multi_season = TRUE) reference site column observation formula (e.g. s(site, bs = "re")) per-site variation enters observation model trend pipeline operates season axis. See ?occ multi-season scope identification caveats. model parameterizes joint cross-species occupancy dynamics. explicit colonization extinction rates.

title: Pivot a detection array to mvgam long-format — pivot_detection_array
code: # Detections of one species at four sites over three visits, laid out # as the `y` slot of an unmarked frame. NA marks a missed visit y <- matrix(c(0, 1, 1,               0, 0, NA,               1, 1, 0,               0, 0, 0), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE) long <- pivot_detection_array(   y,   site_covs = data.frame(forest = c(0.2, 0.8, 0.5, 0.1)),   obs_covs = list(wind = matrix(seq(0.1, 1.2, by = 0.1), nrow = 4)) ) # One row per observed visit. The missed visit is dropped long #>    site visit time y forest wind #> 1     1     1    1 0    0.2  0.1 #> 2     1     2    1 1    0.2  0.5 #> 3     1     3    1 1    0.2  0.9 #> 4     2     1    2 0    0.8  0.2 #> 5     2     2    2 0    0.8  0.6 #> 6     3     1    3 1    0.5  0.3 #> 7     3     2    3 1    0.5  0.7 #> 8     3     3    3 0    0.5  1.1 #> 9     4     1    4 0    0.1  0.4 #> 10    4     2    4 0    0.1  0.8 #> 11    4     3    4 0    0.1  1.2  # Three species in a [species, site, visit] array, as spOccupancy # stores them. Each row names its species in 'series' set.seed(1) y3 <- array(rbinom(36, size = 1, prob = 0.4), dim = c(3, 4, 3)) head(pivot_detection_array(y3, species = c("owl", "hawk", "kite"))) #>   series site visit time y #> 1    owl    1     1    1 0 #> 2    owl    1     2    1 1 #> 3    owl    1     3    1 0 #> 4   hawk    1     1    1 0 #> 5   hawk    1     2    1 0 #> 6   hawk    1     3    1 0  # Next, fit the long frame with mvgam(family = occ())

title: Draws from the Posterior Distribution of an mvgam Model — predict.mvgam
text: type selects quantity returned: "response" (default): draws posterior predictive distribution outcome scale, posterior_predict.mvgam(). "link": linear predictor link scale, posterior_linpred.mvgam(). "expected": expectation E[Y | X] response scale, posterior_epred.mvgam(). "variance": conditional variance Var[Y | theta] per draw, family's mean-variance relation. covers gaussian, student, lognormal, poisson, bernoulli, binomial, negbinomial, gamma beta families. families raise error. default variance observation noise around mean two submodels. process_error = TRUE also conditions draw's sampled trend innovation. "terms": refused pointer functions decompose prediction. posterior_smooths.mvgam() returns per-smooth draws. fixef.mvgam() ranef.mvgam() return parametric random-effect components. "latent_state": closure-unit families, posterior latent state closure unit given detection history: nmix(): latent abundance N given observed visit counts (Royle 2004). occ(): occupancy probability P(z = 1 | y_g). "detection": nmix() occ(), per-visit detection probability \(p_{g,j}\) response scale.

title: Proper scoring rules for mvgam_forecast objects — score.mvgam_forecast
text: "crps" Continuous ranked probability score (Gneiting Raftery 2007) empirical distribution draws. "drps" Discrete ranked probability score, CRPS count summed integer support. "sis" Scaled interval score: width central interval plus penalty observation outside , scaled 2 / (1 - interval_width). "brier" Brier score binary outcome: squared difference observation mean draws. "logs" Log score, -log f(y) kernel density estimate draws. "dss" Dawid-Sebastiani score, depends predictive mean standard deviation alone. "qs" Quantile (pinball) score quantile_level. "twcrps" Threshold-weighted CRPS, scores forecast inside [lower, upper]. "energy" Energy score series jointly. "variogram" Variogram score order 0.5 series jointly (Scheuerer Hamill 2015). "twenergy" Threshold-weighted energy score.

title: Calculate measures of latent VAR community stability — stability.mvgam
text: measures describe much lagged interactions among series contribute variability system. also describe system responds perturbation (Ives et al. 2003). latent VAR(1) $$   x_t \sim \text{MVNormal}(x_{t - 1}, \Sigma)   $$ stationary covariance \(\Sigma_{\infty}\) solves \(\Sigma_{\infty} = \Sigma_{\infty} ^\top + \Sigma\). posterior draw \(\) \(\Sigma\) gives one draw every metric: prop_int: proportion volume stationary distribution lagged interactions generate, \(\det()^2\).   prior \(\) keeps every draw stationary (Heaps 2023). \(\Sigma_{\infty}\) every metric exist every draw. irf() fevd() describe dynamics responses shocks.
code: \item `prop_int_adj`: `prop_int` scaled by the number of series \eqn{p}, \eqn{|\det(A)|^{2/p}}. It compares across systems of different size.  \item `prop_int_offdiag`, `prop_int_diag`: the sensitivity of `prop_int` to each cell of \eqn{A} is \eqn{2 \det(A) (A^{-1})^\top}. `prop_int_offdiag` is the mean absolute sensitivity of the off-diagonal cells (interactions between series) as a share of that mean plus the mean absolute sensitivity of the diagonal cells (self-regulation). `prop_int_diag` is the remaining share.  \item `prop_cov_offdiag`, `prop_cov_diag`: the same split for the sensitivity of \eqn{\det(\Sigma_{\infty})} to each cell of \eqn{\Sigma_{\infty}}, \eqn{\det(\Sigma_{\infty})     (\Sigma_{\infty}^{-1})^\top}. Off-diagonal cells are counted where \eqn{\Sigma} is estimated.  \item `reactivity`: the log of the largest singular value of \eqn{A}, \eqn{\log \sigma_{max}(A)} (Neubert et al. 2009). A positive value means some perturbation grows in the step after it occurs, before the system returns to equilibrium.  \item `mean_return_rate`: the largest modulus of the eigenvalues of \eqn{A}. The distance of the mean from its stationary value shrinks by this factor each step, asymptotically. A value nearer 1 means a slower return.  \item `var_return_rate`: the same factor for the variance, the largest modulus of the eigenvalues of \eqn{A \otimes A}, which is `mean_return_rate` squared.

MG Neubert, H Caswell & AR Solow (2009). Detecting reactivity. Ecology, 90, 2683-2688. SE Heaps (2023). Enforcing stationarity prior vector autoregressions. Journal Computational Graphical Statistics, 32, 74-83.
